newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Kabila to arrive in Kinshasa Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Kabila to arrive in Kinshasa Tuesday.

text.p: The United States expects Laurent Kabila, self-proclaimed president of the new Democratic Republic of Congo, to arrive in the capital Kinshasa and establish a government within 24 hours, the State Department said on Monday.

"We understand, based on meetings this morning, that Mr. Laurent Kabila plans to arrive in Kinshasa tomorrow, that he plans to formally establish an interim government by tomorrow evening," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Burns said U.S. Ambassador Daniel Simpson met Monday morning with two aides to Kabila, Deogratias Bugera and Paul Kabungo, and they agreed to establish "ongoing contacts" between the U.S. embassy in Kinshasa and the new leadership of the central African country.

Burns also said the United States would accept the new name Kabila's forces had given the country and work with the new government that ousted Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko but saw no need to make an official proclamation on this point.

"We will no longer be calling this country Zaire...That country has vanished, and obviously, a new country -- a new government -- is now being established under different people. And we will refer to this country as the Democratic Republic of the Congo," Burns said. "We consider the relationship between the United States and this country to be ongoing."
Earlier, in Harare, South African President Nelson Mandela said Kabila would enter Kinshasa on Tuesday and address his nation.
